answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when the same operator is caught running duplicates. Like light through a prism, one stake splits into verifiable signals — on-chain history, peer attestations, and work output — so a grove of fake accounts cannot share one reputation. Climbing that ridge costs real capital per identity, and duplicates forfeit their deposits, making mass fakery unprofitable while honest agents earn their stake back.
